sentences.text: Palaeotodus is an extinct genus of birds belonging to the todie family Todidae, which includes modern todies. These ancient species were larger than their modern relatives but similar in size to the modern tody motmot.
Remains of Palaeotodus emryi show a larger body size and proportionally larger wings compared to modern todies.
The genus Palaeotodus was described by Olson in 1976, with the species Palaeotodus emryi based on Oligocene fossils from Wyoming.
Two other species were described by Mourer-Chauviré in 1985: Palaeotodus escampsiensis from Upper Eocene fossils in France and Palaeotodus itardiensis from Lower Oligocene fossils in France.
Fossils of Palaeotodus date to the Lower Oligocene epoch, when the genus lived between 33.9 and 27.3 million years ago during the Rupelian stage.
Fossils of Palaeotodus have been found in France and the US state of Wyoming.
